issues.competing_evidence: Catalán+99 main text/equation defines q=M2/M1=0.54±0.14, while Table 4 labels q=M1/M2 and prints 0.54±0.08. Schwope+00 uses Q=M1/M2=1.75; Watson+03 reports q=M2/M1=0.63 under its Roche-tomography assumptions.
issues.why_it_matters: The ratio convention affects inferred component masses and any cross-population comparison.
issues.needed_action: Verify whether Catalán+99 has an erratum or author clarification; until then retain both statements and never use its table q as canonical.

issues.competing_evidence: Optical/tomographic solutions give M1≈0.54–0.66 M_sun, while Cropper+98 Ginga spectral fits give 1.12–1.13 M_sun (90% interval 0.95–1.30). Inclinations conflict: Schwope+00 50–70 deg; Catalán+99 best 65±7 and upper≈72; Watson+03 Table 3 72–90 but prose excludes >72. Cropper (1998) original polarimetry gives approximate i≈50 deg and pole colatitude≈40 deg from a simple geometry argument.
issues.references: MukaiCharles+87_QQVul; Catalan+99_QQVul; Watson+03_RocheTomography; Cropper+98Mass_QQVul; Cropper+98Polarimetry_QQVul; Schwope+00_QQVul
issues.why_it_matters: The selected mass and inclination would materially change QQ Vul’s location in WD-mass comparisons and any evolutionary interpretation.
issues.needed_action: Keep measurements by method separate. Check original Cropper polarimetry and Watson+03 text/table interpretation (or author clarification) before choosing a preferred inclination/mass branch.

issues.competing_evidence: Catalán+99 directly classifies donor as M4V from TiO; Mukai & Charles 1986 gives M2–4 template range; queried SIMBAD record says M2 D with no traceable citation.
issues.why_it_matters: Subtype enters donor-sequence predictions for mass, radius and evolutionary state.
issues.needed_action: Locate the provenance of SIMBAD M2 D and check whether its source predates the direct M4V spectroscopy; keep M4V as the primary measured classification for now.

issues.competing_evidence: Belle+00 states field strength was not directly measured; quotes assumed typical 20–30 MG and indirect <10–30 MG possibility. Ferrario+15 table lists uncertain Bcyc1=30: MG. No primary cyclotron/Zeeman measurement was confirmed.
issues.why_it_matters: Confusing a prior, accretion-region estimate, cyclotron-region field and WD surface field could create a false magnetic-field trend.
issues.needed_action: Obtain and follow the primary citation chain behind Ferrario+15 Bcyc1=30: before using any numeric WD-field value; retain the fields as component-specific claims.

issues.competing_evidence: Barrett+20 reports Stokes I=92±39 uJy (nominal 2.36σ) and a custom combined significance score 36.9 based on a product of distance, flux and polarized-flux terms; RR=0±56 uJy, LL=134±58 uJy and CP=−100±60%. Ridder+23 has no repeat QQ Vul row.
issues.why_it_matters: Counting this as a secure radio detection changes population statistics and radio-luminosity comparisons.
issues.needed_action: For the community catalog, decide whether to label this as published detection / low-significance candidate; preserve Stokes measurements and the paper’s custom score either way.

issues.competing_evidence: QQ Vul is classified as a polar and is conventionally treated as synchronized, but no independent WD spin period was found in inspected papers. Existing compatibility field had stored Porb as spin.
issues.why_it_matters: A synchronism assumption represented as a second independent clock can contaminate spin/orbit distributions.
issues.needed_action: Use the orbital period as measured and leave the independent WD-spin numeric field blank; retain synchronism only as interpretation unless an independent spin measurement is found.

issues.competing_evidence: Cropper (1998) original full text is now retrieved and checked. Sect. 5 gives approximate i≈50 deg and magnetic-pole colatitude beta≈40 deg using simple polarization geometry; not a 40–50 deg interval.
issues.why_it_matters: This primary inclination estimate is part of the competing geometry literature used to interpret mass solutions.

references.note: Downloaded correct arXiv PDF and text-extracted to tmp/pdfs/text/Watson+03_RocheTomography.txt. Roche tomography of secondary stars in AM Her, QQ Vul, IP Peg, and HU Aqr using Na I absorption. For QQ Vul, audited lower inclination limit ~72 deg from entropy reconstructions, exclusion of inclinations >72 deg from lack of X-ray eclipse at phase zero, adopted i=72 deg with M1=0.66 Msun and M2=0.42 Msun, full range M1=0.58-0.66 Msun and M2=0.34-0.44 Msun as inclination increases to 90 deg, and Na I absorption map showing irradiation/shielding of the donor. The paper does not provide WD Teff or magnetic-field strength. HU Aqr audit: Roche tomography gives gamma=7 km/s, q=0.25, best comparison masses M1=0.61 Msun and M2=0.15 Msun, and inclination 84.4 deg using the eclipse width; these are retained only as older comparison values because Schwope+25_HUAqr provides newer direct eclipse/LCURVE masses.
references.full_citation: Watson, C. A., Dhillon, V. S., Rutten, R. G. M., & Schwope, A. D. 2003, Roche tomography of cataclysmic variables – II. Images of the secondary stars in AM Her, QQ Vul, IP Peg and HU Aqr, Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, 341, 129–142.
